clue.text: Meat is cut badly in primitive beginning

indicators.note: the word in tells us the scrambled letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: proto- is the prefix meaning first or primitive, the beginning of a word like prototype

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of is cut come out in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A butcher is mocked for hacking at meat in a crude, primitive way.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosciutto is an Italian dry-cured ham, a kind of meat.

clue.text: Soldier taken by enemy across river in front of boat

indicators.note: the prisoner letters stretch across the river letter, so it sits inside them

parts.note: a POW is a prisoner of war, a soldier captured by the enemy

explanation.surface: A captured soldier is ferried over a river in the bow of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts R inside POW.
explanation.definitionFit: The prow is the pointed front part of a ship or boat.

clue.text: Supervised part of test on tool

parts.note: in a cricket Test match, an over of six balls is one part of the play
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Someone oversaw a trial run of a new tool.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, and an over is a set of six balls bowled. In a down clue, 'on' stacks the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise, so oversaw is the past tense to match.

clue.text: Queer changes in church committee on which bishops and others sit

definitions.text: on which bishops and others sit

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are set inside the other pieces

parts.note: a board is a committee, such as a board of directors

indicators.note: the letters of queer go through changes into a new order

explanation.surface: Strange shifts happen on a church committee where bishops sit.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishops seem to be clergy on a church board, but they are chess pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess board is a chequerboard, and bishops, knights and pawns stand on its squares.

clue.text: Clear a bottleneck in a French port

parts.note: un is French for a
Cork is a port city in southern Ireland

explanation.surface: Traffic jams build up in a French harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottleneck' suggests a traffic jam; read literally it is the neck of a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncork a bottle is to clear its neck by drawing out the stopper.

clue.text: Classic material for shipbuilding

definitions.meaning: one of the five English Classics, the flat horse races for three-year-olds
oak timbers were the traditional wood for building sailing ships

explanation.definitionFit: The Oaks is a Classic horse race at Epsom; oaks, the trees, gave the wood for ships.

clue.text: Later broadcast that is kept within studio

indicators.note: the abbreviation is kept inside the scrambled letters
something broadcast is scattered, so the letters of later are spread into a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A programme is broadcast later from the studio where it was recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio or workshop.

clue.text: Allow, for example, what came first

parts.note: say is used to mean for example, as in 'a fruit, say, an apple'
St John's Gospel begins 'In the beginning was the Word', so the Word came first

explanation.surface: Someone asks permission, for instance, by pointing to what came first.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gospel of John opens 'In the beginning was the Word', which is why 'what came first' is THE WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: To say the word is an idiom for giving permission or the go-ahead, so it means allow.

clue.text: Get carried away and wildly exert voice

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the verb: to stir someone so much that they get carried away

indicators.note: letters treated wildly are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loses control and starts shouting at the top of their voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges the ten letters of EXERT VOICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To overexcite is to stir up too much, making someone lose their self-control.

clue.text: Site of cathedral on river bank

indicators.note: in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y, so the cathedral city comes after the river letter

parts.note: Ely is a small city in Cambridgeshire with a famous cathedral

explanation.surface: A cathedral stands on the bank of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a riverbank in the picture, but it is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to rely on them, so the verb bank is a synonym.

clue.text: Encourages saint to make this dish

parts.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them
St Benedict founded the Benedictine order of monks

explanation.surface: A cook urges a saint to make a particular dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Encourages' gives EGGS through the phrase 'eggs on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs Benedict is a brunch dish of poached eggs and ham on a muffin with hollandaise sauce.

clue.text: Speech from big mouth?

parts.note: a big mouth is a river's wide mouth meeting the sea, here the Thames, so this is the way of speaking from the area around it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Big mouth' suggests a loudmouth, but the mouth is the Thames estuary, and the speech is the accent of London and south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the Thames estuary, it is the accent spoken around London and the south-east of England.

clue.text: Fireman from Maine supporting all the minute, states around

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Fireman from Maine supporting all the minute, states around': PRO + ME + THE + US fits, but 'all' and 'minute' give no letters that fit and nothing supplies PRO, so the clue looks garbled; the scan is blank.

clue.text: As prize, bring back something attractive?

indicators.note: bringing a word back means reading it from end to start

parts.note: a drawer is something that draws, that is, attracts people

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves a magnet as their prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring back' reverses DRAWER, a thing that draws people in. The question mark flags that odd sense of drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a prize given for some achievement.

clue.text: Plant parts of garden, reversing ugly growth

parts.note: flower beds are parts of a garden

indicators.note: reversing means the word for the growth is written backwards

parts.note: a wart is an unsightly growth on the skin

explanation.surface: A gardener tries to stop unsightly growth spreading through the beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns WART into TRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedstraw is a wild plant of the genus Galium, once used to stuff mattresses.

clue.text: Compromise rated?

parts.note: the clue word is what you get when trade is sent off into a new arrangement, off acting as the anagram signal

explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the answer TRADE OFF tells you to scramble TRADE, which gives 'rated'. The question mark flags this reverse clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-off is a compromise where something is given up to gain something else.

clue.text: Fail to notice our current state

parts.note: to miss something is to fail to notice it
taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Someone fails to see what is going on in their own day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like an adjective meaning present, but it gives I, the physics symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Performed tune the wrong way? It's not just wine

parts.note: sang means performed as a singer

indicators.note: going the wrong way, the word for tune runs backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A singer gets a song backwards at a party where more than wine is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine mixed with fruit and other ingredients, so it is more than plain wine.

clue.text: African type I repeatedly kept away from disease

indicators.note: letters kept away from a word are taken out of it

parts.note: beriberi is a disease caused by lack of vitamin B1

indicators.note: repeatedly means the letter I is used twice

explanation.surface: Someone stays clear of an infection that keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I repeatedly' means two Is; 'kept away from' takes both out of BERIBERI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berbers are a people of North Africa, so a Berber is one African type.

clue.text: Big mule maltreated in this country

indicators.note: the letters of big mule are roughly handled into a new order

explanation.surface: A large mule is badly treated in a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maltreated' rearranges BIG MULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgium is a country in western Europe.

clue.text: Explain one's view of shark in river

indicators.note: the fin piece goes inside the river name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
a shark's fin breaking the water is often all anyone sees of it

explanation.surface: Someone describes catching sight of a shark in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To define something is to explain exactly what it means.

clue.text: Cask composer and author found in Kentish town

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer
Frank Bridge was an English composer, teacher of Benjamin Britten
H. G. Wells was the author of The War of the Worlds

explanation.surface: A barrel, a musician and a writer all turn up in a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunbridge Wells is a spa town in the county of Kent.

clue.text: Burden borne by university's old group of students

parts.note: the NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK students' organisation

explanation.surface: A university's old students' society carries a heavy responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility that falls on someone.

clue.text: Time to introduce final character in book

indicators.note: the time word takes in the letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: an era is a period of time
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An author holds back the last character until late in the novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final character' looks like a person in a story, but it is the last letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: If one stands long enough, will one get a seat?

definitions.text: If one stands long enough, will one get a seat?

parts.words: If one stands long enough, will one get a seat?
parts.note: reads like a commuter on a crowded train, but standing means running as a candidate and a seat means a place in parliament

explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a rush-hour passenger waiting to sit; the other sense of 'stands' is standing for election.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician stands for election in the hope of winning a seat in parliament.

clue.text: Strike does for big contract

definitions.meaning: to hit something hard, as in slamming a door or a fist
in bridge a small or grand ... is a bid to take all or all but one of the tricks

explanation.definitionFit: To slam is to strike hard; in bridge a slam is a contract to win nearly every trick.
